chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ammar Bin Marwan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), said:

I said to him, 'A man came to a woman and asked her to marry herself to him. She said, 'I marry myself to you on the condition that you seek from me whatever you wish of looking or touching, and attain from me what a man attains from his wife, except that you do not enter your private part into my private part, and you enjoy whatever you wish, for I fear the loss of virginity (or exposure).' He said, 'He has only what was stipulated.'

key_terms.تُزَوِّجَهُ نَفْسَهَا: She marries herself to him (self-marriage contract)
key_terms.فَرْجَكَ فِي فَرْجِي: Entering your private part into my private part (intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a marriage contract where intercourse is explicitly excluded by the wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'shurut al-nisa' (women's stipulations) in Shia jurisprudence, where a specific condition excluding vaginal intercourse (dakhil al-farj) remains valid and binding on the husband. It highlights the flexibility of the marital contract, allowing couples to tailor rights and obligations, provided the core essence of marriage is not entirely negated. The ruling underscores that explicit stipulations take precedence, offering a practical framework for consensual arrangements that prioritize mutual agreement over default legal presumptions.
